contributions.headingText: Localized mesothelioma is a rare malignant neoplasm of mesothelial cell origin that occurs as a circumscribed mass with no clinical or histological evidence of diffuse serosal spread.

Acceptable: localized mesothelioma.

Not recommended: localized malignant mesothelioma; solitary malignant mesothelioma.
Epithelioid mesothelioma; sarcomatoid mesothelioma (including desmoplastic); biphasic mesothelioma

Most cases (82–88%) occur as an intrathoracic mass localized to the pleura, chest wall, lung, or mediastinum {31485011}. Extrathoracic sites of origin include the abdominal wall, fallopian tube, gastric serosa, hepatic capsule, tunica albuginea, and broad ligament.

Patients can be asymptomatic or present with chest pain, dyspnoea, or other symptoms related to compression of various structures {31485011}. Imaging studies reveal a mass lesion that is clinically suspicious for sarcoma or metastasis to the serosal membranes {26770440}.

The tumour is rare and poorly recognized; approximately 160 cases have been reported {31485011}. Men are more often affected than women (M:F ratio: 2.7:1). Patients range in age from 6 to 82 years, with a mean age of 59 years.

Localized mesothelioma appears to show a loose association with exposure to asbestos. Approximately 37% of the reported patients have a history of asbestos exposure, which, in general, is poorly documented with no clear characterization of the fibre type and levels of exposure {31485011}.
BAP1 mutations, TRAF7 mutations, and genomic near-haploidization have recently been described as potential pathogenetic pathways in localized mesothelioma {31371807}.
Localized mesothelioma is a solitary, circumscribed mass attached to the pleura or other serosal surfaces {26770440}.

The histopathological, ultrastructural, and immunophenotypic features of localized mesothelioma are identical to those of diffuse mesothelioma {7511353; 15958850; 30798074; 31485011}. Approximately 55% of the tumours are epithelioid lesions; others exhibit biphasic or sarcomatoid morphology. Rare epithelioid localized mesotheliomas with pleomorphic, microcystic, and rhabdoid features have also been described. Occasional sarcomatoid tumours showed desmoplastic or lymphohistiocytoid differentiation.

Immunohistochemistry

Immunohistochemistry is the same as in diffuse mesothelioma.

Differential diagnosis

The differential diagnosis includes solitary fibrous tumour (see section Solitary fibrous tumour of the thorax), metastatic carcinoma and sarcoma (see section Metastasis to the pleura), primary pleural and peripherally located pulmonary synovial and other sarcomas (see section Synovial sarcoma of the thorax), and diffuse mesothelioma (see section Diffuse pleural mesothelioma).

FNA can be diagnostic of localized mesothelioma, especially the epithelioid subtype, by revealing malignant cells identical to those described in diffuse mesothelioma (see section Diffuse pleural mesothelioma). Pleural fluid cytology should be negative for malignant cells in these patients by definition {31485011}.
Diagnostic molecular pathology is the same as for diffuse mesothelioma (see section Diffuse pleural mesothelioma).

Essential:

  • Presentation as a solitary localized mass by imaging, surgical findings, and histology
  • Examination of a surgical resection specimen showing lack of invasion beyond the circumscribed borders of the tumour
  • Histological features of diffuse mesothelioma
  • Immunohistochemical evidence of mesothelial origin

Desirable:

  • Multidisciplinary discussion to confirm the diagnosis
Staging is the same as for diffuse pleural mesothelioma.

Patients are usually treated with surgical resection {18155556}, which is sometimes supplemented by chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy {31485011}. In earlier series, the median survival time of patients with localized mesothelioma reported in the English-language literature ranged from 12 to 36 months, with a pooled median survival time of 29 months {23328002}. However, in a more recent study, for 51 localized mesothelioma patients diagnosed by the International Mesothelioma Panel, the median survival time was 134 months {31485011}. Patients with complete resection and epithelioid histology have a better prognosis than those with postsurgical residual disease and/or sarcomatoid or biphasic histology.
